po_authorization_ref: Executed under the existing D35 decision. The Product Owner authorized completion of the remaining repository-only Fresh Production readiness work -- closing the two blockers recorded by T0076 -- before any appliance deployment, and directed that the state advance to READY_FOR_FRESH_PRODUCTION_APPLIANCE_DEPLOYMENT only once those blockers are verified closed. previous_state_note: T0076 recorded the factory-clean install path as hardened but carrying two Production-readiness blockers: iam_v2 objects created by migrations 0009+ were left owned by the platform role in a clean build, and the superseded guest-auth authority remained selectable by configuration.
new_state_note: Both blockers are CLOSED and verified semantically in a clean-room build from an empty isolated environment on the Production-equivalent image, through the real Gate-P path. Ownership is now asserted by deploy/gatep/gatep-iam-ownership.sql as an explicit install step before the grants, so the privilege bootstrap lands on the final ownership state; it fails closed on any object it cannot converge and on any SECURITY DEFINER function left executing as the wrong owner. The guest IAM authority is locked on the production profile by data-plane/internal/iamv2/guest_authority_lock.go: an explicit attempt to disable IAM-v2 for vouchers or accounts, and the master switch being off, are both STARTUP REFUSALS rather than silent downgrades. The verifier proves ownership by asking the catalog, names any exception instead of counting it, reports ownership as an ordinary catalog fact, and re-runs the authority-lock tests, so neither property is asserted only by the thing being tested.
blockers_closed: OWNERSHIP -- CLOSED. deploy/gatep/gatep-iam-ownership.sql reassigns every table, view, materialised view, sequence, function and procedure in iam_v2 to iam_v2_owner, takes the schema itself, and asserts both outcomes fail-closed. Clean-room result: every iam_v2 object owned by iam_v2_owner; all 67 SECURITY DEFINER functions in iam_v2 execute as iam_v2_owner; schema iam_v2 owned by iam_v2_owner.

CONFIGURATION-SELECTABLE LEGACY AUTHORITY -- CLOSED for the production runtime. enforceGuestAuthorityLock is applied inside LoadConfigFromEnv on the production profile that edged and scd already pass. STAYCONNECT_IAMV2_VOUCHER or _ACCOUNT set to false/0 is a startup refusal naming the exact variable; the master switch cannot be off; with nothing configured both locked methods come up as IAM-v2. OTP and social remain configurable because they reach external providers gated by their own decisions, and can only ever be configured on, never redirected to a superseded implementation. Development and test builds keep the configurable behaviour, so the accepted DEVELOPMENT trial evidence remains reproducible.

bounded_dependency_review.method: read-only inbound foreign-key, view and function inspection on the development appliance, plus a repository reference count for each object
bounded_dependency_review.outcome: PHYSICAL REMOVAL NOT PROVABLE IN THIS PASS AND THEREFORE NOT DONE. public.payments and public.social_oauth_states are CURRENT and still foreign-key into ticket_templates and vouchers, so dropping those parents today would break code that is not superseded. Per the instruction to remove superseded tables only after proving no current required dependency, that proof does not hold and the tables stay. Migrating payments and social_oauth_states onto IAM-v2 parents is the prerequisite and is its own bounded work item. No view or function references the superseded set.
bounded_dependency_review.claim_being_made: a fresh Production appliance creates these tables EMPTY and no configuration can make them the guest authority, so it has zero superseded ACTIVE runtime dependency for guest IAM. The claim is not that the tables do not exist.
